summary: LLM inference costs scale directly with token consumption, and unoptimized production apps routinely overspend by 50-80% on redundant context, verbose prompts, oversized models, and repeated API calls. Applying a layered set of techniques—prompt caching, semantic caching, model cascading, and prompt compression—typically cuts inference spend by 50-90% while often improving latency. Most of these wins are low-risk engineering changes that require no model retraining.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Cache the static prefix of prompts (system instructions, few-shot examples, documents) so the provider skips reprocessing unchanged input tokens on repeated calls. Supported natively by major providers, billed at a heavily discounted rate for cached tokens.
techniques.savings: up to 90% reduction on repeated input tokens
techniques.example: Place your long, unchanging system prompt and RAG context at the start of every request so Anthropic/OpenAI charge cached-token rates (~10% of normal) for that prefix on subsequent calls within the cache TTL.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Store past query-response pairs and serve a cached answer when a new query is semantically similar (via embedding similarity) instead of calling the LLM again. Hit rates of 60-70% are common for repetitive workloads.
techniques.savings: 40-70% reduction (eliminates calls entirely on cache hits)
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache to embed incoming questions; if cosine similarity to a stored question exceeds 0.95, return the cached answer instead of hitting the model.

techniques.name: Model Cascading / Routing
techniques.description: Route easy or low-stakes requests to small, cheap models and escalate only hard requests to large expensive models. A cheap model handles the bulk, a strong model acts as fallback when confidence is low.
techniques.savings: 50-80% reduction in average cost per request
techniques.example: Send all queries to GPT-4o-mini first and only re-run with GPT-4o when the mini response's self-reported confidence or a judge score falls below a threshold.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduce prompt length by removing redundancy, trimming few-shot examples, and compressing context with tools like LLMLingua that drop low-information tokens while preserving meaning.
techniques.example: Run retrieved RAG chunks through LLMLingua-2 to compress a 2,000-token context down to ~800 tokens before sending it to the model, keeping key facts intact.

techniques.name: Output Token Control
techniques.description: Cap and constrain generated output since output tokens are often 2-4x more expensive than input tokens. Use max_tokens limits, structured/JSON output, and instructions to be concise.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and instruct the model to 'answer in one sentence, no preamble' for classification tasks to avoid paying for rambling responses.

techniques.name: Right-Sizing the Model
techniques.description: Pick the smallest model that meets quality requirements for each task rather than defaulting to the flagship model everywhere. Evaluate cheaper tiers and open-source models on your actual eval set.
techniques.savings: 50-90% reduction versus using a top-tier model for all tasks
techniques.example: Migrate extraction and summarization tasks from GPT-4o to GPT-4o-mini or Llama-3.1-8B after confirming comparable accuracy on a 100-example benchmark.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Combine multiple independent requests into a single call or use provider batch APIs that offer ~50% discounts for asynchronous, non-time-sensitive workloads.
techniques.savings: up to 50% reduction for async workloads
techniques.example: Submit nightly bulk classification jobs through the OpenAI Batch API to get a 50% per-token discount with results returned within 24 hours.

techniques.name: Streaming and Early Stopping
techniques.description: Stream responses and stop generation as soon as the required content is produced, using stop sequences and application-level cutoffs to avoid generating unnecessary tokens.
techniques.savings: 10-30% reduction in output tokens; improved perceived latency
techniques.example: Define stop=['\n\n'] so the model halts after the first paragraph when only a short answer is needed.

techniques.name: RAG Context Pruning
techniques.description: Retrieve fewer, higher-quality chunks and rerank to send only the most relevant context, rather than stuffing many documents into the prompt.
techniques.example: Retrieve top-20 chunks, rerank with a cross-encoder, and pass only the top-3 to the LLM instead of dumping all 20 into the context window.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic cache for LLM queries that stores and reuses responses based on embedding similarity, integrating with LangChain and major providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open-source, Apache 2.0); you pay only for the backing vector/cache store you host

tools.name: Redis / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: In-memory data store with vector search used to build low-latency semantic caches and exact prompt caches for LLM apps.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; Redis Cloud from ~$5/mo, usage-based scaling for managed tiers

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy and SDK that normalizes 100+ LLM providers behind one OpenAI-style API, with built-in caching, routing, fallbacks, and spend tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; LiteLLM Enterprise custom pricing for SSO, support, and admin features

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing request logging, cost tracking, caching, and rate limiting via a one-line proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); Pro from ~$20/mo, usage-based and enterprise plans

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Framework for building LLM applications with built-in support for prompt caching, semantic caching backends, model routing, and RAG pipelines.

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression toolkit that reduces prompt tokens by up to 20x while preserving task performance.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering caching (simple and semantic), load balancing, fallbacks, routing, and observability across multiple LLM providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier available; paid plans from ~$49/mo plus enterprise pricing

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference engine with PagedAttention and prefix caching for cost-efficient self-hosted serving of open models.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open-source, Apache 2.0); you pay only for GPU infrastructure

quick_wins: Enable native prompt caching and put your static system prompt and context at the start of every request to cut repeated input costs by up to 90%.
Switch default tasks from flagship models to smaller tiers (e.g., GPT-4o-mini, Llama-3.1-8B) after a quick eval, saving 50-90% with minimal quality loss.
Set tight max_tokens limits and instruct models to be concise, since output tokens are the most expensive part of a request.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of repetitive query workloads to serve 40-70% of requests without calling the model.
Route non-urgent bulk jobs through provider Batch APIs for an immediate ~50% per-token discount.
